{{Short description|Russian mathematician (1938–2023)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
'''Aleksei Viktorovich Chernavskii''' (or '''Chernavsky''' or '''Černavskii''') ({{langx|ru|Алексей Викторович Чернавский}}; 17 January 1938 – 22 December 2023) was a Russian mathematician, specializing in differential geometry and topology.

==Biography==
Chernavskii was born in [[Moscow]] and completed undergraduate study at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics of [[Moscow State University]] in 1959. He enrolled in graduate school at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]. In 1964 he defended his [[Candidate of Sciences]] (PhD) thesis, written under the guidance of [[Lyudmila Keldysh]], on the topic Конечнократные отображения многообразий (Finite-fold mappings of manifolds). In 1970 he defended his Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] (habilitation) thesis Гомеоморфизмы и топологические вложения многообразий (Homeomorphisms and topological embeddings of manifolds).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=95090}}</ref> In 1970 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Nice.<ref>{{cite book|author=Černavskii, A. V.|chapter=Espace de plongements|title=Internat. Congr. Math, Nice, 1970|volume=2|year=1970|pages=65–67}}</ref>

Chernavskii worked as a senior researcher at the Steklov Institute until 1973 and from 1973 to 1980 at [[Yaroslavl State University]]. From 1980 to 1985 he was a senior researcher at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].
From 1985 he was employed the [[Kharkevich Institute for Information Transmission Problems]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexey Chernavsky|website=Institute for Information Transmission Problems (Kharkevich Institute)|url=http://iitp.ru/en/users/276.htm}}</ref> From 1993 he was working part-time as a professor at the Department of Higher Geometry and Topology, Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics, Moscow State University. He wrote a textbook on differential geometry for advanced students.<ref>{{cite book| author = Чернавский, А. В.  | chapter = | chapter-url = | format = | url = http://higeom.math.msu.su/people/chernavski/chernav-difgeom2011.pdf | title = Дифференциальная геометрия, 2 курс | orig-year = | agency =  | edition =   |location=  |date = 2012 |publisher=  |at=  |volume=  | pages = | page =  | series =  | isbn = }}</ref>

Chernavskii died on 22 December 2023, at the age of 85.<ref>[https://math.msu.ru/node/2099 Скончался А.В.Чернавский] {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

==Chernavskii's theorem==
'''Chernavskii's theorem''' (1964): If <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> are ''n''-manifolds and <math>f</math> is a discrete, open, continuous mapping of <math>M</math> into <math>N</math><br>then the branch set <math>B</math><sub><math>f</math></sub> = { x: x is an element of <math>M</math> and <math>f</math> fails to be a local homeomorphism at x} satisfies dimension (<math>B</math><sub><math>f</math></sub>) ≤ ''n'' – 2.<ref>{{cite web|author=Martio, O.|author2=Ryazanov|title=The Chernavskii Theorem and Embedding Dimension (preprint)|date=19 October 1999|website=wiki.helsinki.fi|url=https://wiki.helsinki.fi/download/attachments/33885362/Preprint179.ps}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Chernavskii, A. V.|year=1964|title=Finite-to-one open mappings of manifolds (Russian)|journal=Mat. Sb. |series=Novaya Seriya  |volume=65(107)|issue=3|pages=357–369|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/eng/msb4483|postscript=; Amer. Math. Soc. Trans. (2) 100 1972, 253–257}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Chernavskii, A. V.|year=1965|title=Addendum to the paper "Finite-to-one open mappings of manifolds" (Russian)|journal=Mat. Sb. |series=Novaya Seriya |volume=66(108)|issue=3|pages=471–472|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/eng/msb4330|postscript=; Amer. Math. Soc. Trans. (2) 100 1972, 296–270}}</ref>
